5. Cite the full published rational-root theorem for rational algebraic integers.

7. Narrow the order-\(\le15\) example to Sylow data rather than claiming an unsupported isomorphism classification.

Exact old/new scaffold text and decline consequences are in the notes.

### Richness and decomposition

Both decomposition and corollary passes were performed separately for each pair.

The Sylow development decomposes Sylow I, finite nilpotence, Fitting/Frattini machinery, and the normal-Sylow applications into focused lemmas. Added corollaries cover uniqueness/normality, the Frattini–Fitting inclusion, and nonsimplicity for orders \(p^2q\) and \(pq\).

The module development separates the isomorphism theorems, chain-condition equivalences, exact-sequence inheritance, Jordan–Hölder, endomorphism-ring machinery, semisimple equivalences, and the radical-free Wedderburn–Artin route. Added corollaries cover finite sums, Hopficity, length additivity, left/right semisimplicity, chain conditions for semisimple rings, and integrality consequences.

Neither A page approaches the 60-item ceiling closely enough to justify a split.

Primary treatments include [Conrad on Sylow](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/grouptheory/sylowpf.pdf), [Boston on Fitting and Frattini subgroups](https://people.math.wisc.edu/~nboston/notes3.pdf), [Crawley-Boevey on noncommutative algebra](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~wcrawley/1617noncommalg/Noncommutative%20algebra.pdf), [MIT 18.706 on semisimple modules](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-706-noncommutative-algebra-spring-2023/mit18_706_s23_lec02.pdf), and [Grifo on integrality](https://eloisagrifo.github.io/Teaching/ca1/CA1notes.pdf).
